title: Fix the recent ratings strip
prompt: The home page shows the eight newest ratings, newest first. The function below was written for it, but it shows old ratings in the wrong order. Fix `solve(ratings)`.
rules: Return every column of `ratings`, unchanged, for the eight ratings with the latest `rated_at`.
Newest first. Ratings made at the same moment are sorted by `user_id`, then by `movie_id`, both from A to Z.
Keep rows exactly as they are, duplicates included. A table with fewer than eight ratings returns all of them.
hints: Press Run: the rows come from the top of the table, not the newest ones. Look at what runs first.
`limit(8)` keeps the first eight rows it comes to. Sort first, then limit.
`orderBy("rated_at")` sorts oldest first. Use `F.col("rated_at").desc()`, and add the two tie-breaking columns.
explanation: The starter limits before it sorts, so it takes eight rows from wherever they happen to be, then sorts those eight; and it sorts oldest first. Swap the steps and reverse the order: `ratings.orderBy(F.col("rated_at").desc(), "user_id", "movie_id").limit(8)`. The tie-breakers make the order unique when two ratings share a moment. `orderBy("rated_at", "user_id", "movie_id", ascending=False)` looks close but sorts the tie-breakers Z to A as well. Each column can get its own direction with `F.col(...).desc()` or `.asc()`.
